minutes.headline: Commission backed an earth-removal permit letter, new loop trails on Holden Wood land, and a 3-year extension at 351 Mass Ave.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard an earth removal (sand) permit review, a proposal to add trails on Holden Wood conservation land, and a request to extend an order of conditions. Much of the meeting was about staffing and administrative gaps: no MUNIS access for the office, Google Drive permissions, and unclear task ownership among new part-time administrators. Roll-call votes were taken on the permit letter, trails, the extension and adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment on the earth removal permit; no hands from the public were seen.
Chair noted no members of the public on the Holden Wood trails item.

votes.motion: Bob to write a letter to the select board saying the earth removal permit involves no activity within the commission's jurisdiction and the commission has no negative comments
Approve creation of new trails on Lunenburg conservation property and authorize Bob to speak with Shirley about connections on Shirley land
Approve extension of the order of conditions at 351 Mass Ave for three additional years

budget_items.what_was_said: The check from the estate was received, larger than initially expected. A fund number and MUNIS access are still needed before it can be spent, and the town attorney said select board approval may be needed to spend it.
An additional cost for cedar siding replacement was confirmed to include chimney flashing repair. The project is near its end.
A vendor approved to replace carpeting at the house remains unpaid because a purchase order has not been submitted. The office lacks MUNIS access.
The commission was not enrolled as members this year, so classes would be taken as non-members and reimbursed by the town.
The commission is sponsoring materials for a kiosk; purchase order coverage was questioned and delivery is delayed until November.
An award has been formalized with the federal authority; paperwork remains to be completed.

budget_items.what_was_said: About 5,000 cubic yards of sand is a byproduct of leveling a field for planting.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to extend the order of conditions at 351 Mass Ave for three additional years.
The commission voted to create new trails on town conservation land and authorized a member to speak with Shirley about connecting trails.
The commission voted to send the select board a letter saying the earth removal permit involves no activity within its jurisdiction and it has no negative comments.
The office still lacks MUNIS access, which leaves a carpeting vendor unpaid and a bequest from an estate unspendable until a fund number is set up.
Enforcement items were sorted: 390 Howard Street silt runoff went to other town departments, and a 176 Elmwood Road compliance certificate was deferred.

why_it_matters: The office cannot pay vendors or spend a bequest left to conservation without MUNIS access and a fund number, which touches how quickly town-held conservation money can be used.
Trail and permit decisions shape how conservation land is used, and pending enforcement items, such as silt runoff, are being handed to other town departments rather than resolved by the commission.
watch_next: Whether MUNIS access is restored to the office's accounts and whether the select board must approve spending the estate bequest (discussed around t=1028 and t=3609).
The commission's requested master checklist of pending enforcement actions and who handles each (t=2856).
